means: Lossy, policy-driven reduction of a text blob to a skeleton of kept spans and omission markers; pure function, full blob stays behind its handle.
The output of striping: one header line, then kept spans interleaved with omission markers, parseable back to source offsets.
A substring of the source retained verbatim in a skeleton; never adjacent to another kept span, never empty.
Single-line placeholder [~N,wW,lL,kX] for an omitted run: UTF-16 unit count, then words, newlines, kind sketch above a size threshold.
Marker detail k: letters, digits, punctuation, whitespace-only or mixed, by share of non-space chars in the omitted run.
Plain object choosing mode, budget, protect patterns, keep-first/last, class override and known terms; every key optional, restrictions off by default.
Pure function (text, policy) to shorter text with a header; squeeze, keyword lines, head and tail, and striping are all reducers.
Versioned name of one reducer behaviour, such as stripe-1.0; a changed byte is a new id and ids are never reused.
Notional label in the skeleton header, derived from line features (list, headed, json, code, log, tabular, prose, mixed), selecting the cue profile.
Weight of a unit by how few segments hold it, whole blob and local window, in smoothed df arithmetic (Zipf and IDF-shaped).
Header suffix seen[ PCT%] telling the model this blob was already reduced, with the same policy (header only) or another cut.
Smallest run a skeleton may keep: 2 chars, 3 once its adjacent delimiter is attached; shorter unprotected runs are dropped.
Kept source units over source length, reported as pct in the header; distinct from the output-length budget, which counts header and markers.
Monotone post-selection pass: attach adjacent delimiters, fill gaps under minGap, drop short kept runs; makes retained sets nest as budget grows.

name: text striping reducer
claim: A lossy striping reducer (stripe-1.0, docs/STRIPE.md) at equal output chars keeps at least 2x the rare (df-1) units and 1.5x the identifier and number units that the head-and-tail `ends` reducer keeps, and lets a cheap model answer what a stored result is about and which identifiers it names with fewer output_read drill-ins; refuted if either ratio falls under 1.2x or the model needs more drill-ins (cf handles ndgwdh, stems gruwry; baseline outstore ends).

name: striped skeleton notation
claim: The skeleton notation (one header line; kept spans and [~N,wW,lL,kX] markers; `[~` escaped as `[~~`) parses back to the exact source offsets with verify true on 100% of a repo corpus and no collision with markdown or code, at under 30% marker overhead on blobs over 2000 chars; refuted by one failed parse-back or by marker cost above that share (cf ambiguous markers hzzgju; tenet 30, single-line markers).

name: lexical rarity heuristics
claim: Smoothed document-frequency rarity over whole blob and 25-segment windows, plus structure cues (headings, signal words, identifiers, numbers, keys, line leads), ranks what to keep better than head-and-tail position and than a pure global-rank (Zipf) score, in pure arithmetic with byte-identical output across engines; refuted if rank or IDF-with-logs retains more rare and identifier units at equal chars (docs/STRIPE.md 2.2, open question 16).

name: reducer class record
claim: A notional class label in the skeleton header (list, headed, json, code, log, tabular, prose, mixed), derived deterministically from line features, picks a cue profile that retains more of the units a reader of that class needs (log lead tokens, json keys) than the class-neutral profile at equal chars; refuted if the class-neutral profile retains as much, or if the label disagrees with the features it was derived from (docs/STRIPE.md 5.1).

name: analyzed-before indicator
claim: A `seen` suffix on the skeleton header, set by the caller from a blob-id map, lets a model skip a blob it already holds (header-only form) or read a different cut as new (seen PCT% form), cutting repeated output_read calls and repeated skeleton tokens on re-shown blobs; refuted if repeats do not fall or the model misreads the suffix (cf query shape as the synopsis vtpcxq; docs/STRIPE.md 5.2).
